item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.description: Thu., May 26, 2022; Columbus, Ohio, USA; A person holds an Inclusive Rainbow flag as about 50 protesters gather outside the Ohio Statehouse as lawmakers debate two bills aimed at health care rights. Bickel/Columbus Dispatch News Health Bills Protest Washington voters approved a ban on transgender girls competing in girls’ school sports in last week’s election. But the measure is already facing a legal challenge before it can even take effect. Parents of student athletes, along with the state’s teachers’ union and a trans advocacy group, have filed a lawsuit to block Initiative 638. The suit argues that the measure is discriminatory and that its sex verification requirement could subject girls to “invasive” genital examinations. Initiative 638 Initiative 638 passed with about 56% of the vote last week, even as Democrats made major gains across the country. Similar measures also passed in Arizona, Colorado, and Nebraska. The Washington measure was funded by conservative hedge fund manager Brian Heywood, and supporters argued that it protects fairness in girls’ sports. But voters in a progressive state backing it came as a surprise to many, with the Seattle Times reporting that it likely won votes from some Democrats. Critics have taken particular issue with the measure’s sex verification requirement. Girls who want to join girls’ teams must provide documentation from a medical provider confirming their sex, through hormone or genetic tests or examinations of their “reproductive anatomy,” per the Guardian . The rule does not apply to boys. It also argues that the ban violates a state anti-discrimination law that protects trans people. The plaintiffs include the parent of a 17-year-old trans girl who plays sports at her high school, as well as parents of two cisgender female athletes who oppose the sex verification requirement. item.title: Analysis: No. 23 BYU bests Queens in prolific 3-point party
item.description: BYU forward Bruce Branch III (3) goes up for a shot against Queens of Charlotte during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game, Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, in Provo, Utah. | Rob Gray If you like 3-pointers, hopefully you were watching BYU face Queens on Tuesday night. The Cougars and Royals combined for 31 made triples at the Marriott Center, where BYU came out on top for a 98-82 victory to notch a 3-0 start to the season. A November buy game with 180 total points? Outside of a ranked matchup, that’s about as electric an outing you’ll find at this point in the calendar. There were 134 total shot attempts and 150 offensive possessions between BYU and Queens. The pace of play was outrageous. It was just as much a track meet as it was a basketball game. Eight different Cougars hit 3-pointers, with seven netting multiple makes. Jaxon Kohler and Nate Pickens provided three triples apiece, and BYU’s 17 made threes fell just two shy of the program’s single-game record. “It’s super fun. I mean, we have so many talented shooters,” BYU point guard Rob Wright III said postgame. “Anytime you (shoot), you just know the ball’s probably going in, so we just try and trust each other and keep building that trust and we know the shots are going to keep falling.” Finishing 17 of 37 from behind the arc, the Cougars have now made exactly 46% of their threes in every game this season — a feat that’s as odd as it is elite. “Obviously, when a ball goes through the net, you’re happy with it. I think the efficiency is what I get the most excited about,” BYU head coach Kevin Young said. “But I still feel a little frustration where I think we’re leaving money on the table. This team’s secret sauce is going to be to play unselfishly, and when we do that, I think we’re going to score a lot of points. “... item.description: ATLANTA - DECEMBER 7: Tailback Musa Smith #32 of the University of Georgia Bulldogs carries the ball against the University of Arkansas Razorbacks during the SEC Championship game at the Georgia Dome on December 7, 2002 in Atlanta, Georgia. The Bulldogs defeated the Razorbacks 30-3. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yep, this is one of those nostalgic weeks. This comes thanks to the infinite wisdom of expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams. That, as is well known, means that next month’s SEC Championship will now officially be the final one. For Georgia fans, playing in this event has become commonplace, but it was not always this way. In fact, until 2002, each December meant lots of watching other SEC rivals take their turn in the spotlight with Georgia fans left to wonder when that time would come..if ever. For that reason, its why when you think back to the most memorable SEC title game for Georgia, 2002 outranks them all. The whole week was a Mardi Gras for Georgia fans. Thanks to Arkansas’ enthusiasm being grossly outweighed by Georgia fans, the whole scene around the Georgia Dome was a red and black party, and the result was a foregone conclusion. Yes, there have been other sweet wins in this game for Georgia with last year’s long-awaited win against Bama and the victory a year prior against Texas. The revenge win against Auburn was satisfying, as were the separate wins against LSU, but it terms of what it meant for Georgia fans – the Arkansas win, at least from this viewpoint, will always rank at the top. In reality, the loss of the SEC title game is a microcosm of the path being driven for college football. And aren’t you glad that teams are going to be incentivized to play marquee games? item.title: Leeds United pair join combat veterans for special Remembrance event
item.description: Leeds United pair join combat veterans for special Remembrance event Brenden Aaronson and Tarik Muharemović joined veterans to lay wreaths and observe two minutes of silence at Elland Road, before a visit to the Combat Cafe. The first team pair were special guests of a Leeds United Foundation social group that meets once a week at the stadium. "Anybody can get involved to come along and just speak to people," said Derek McHugh, a 22-year Coldstream Guards army veteran. "That's all it is. It's a group that speaks to one another, and we get support from the the club as well, especially the staff that come every week. If we need support, we can speak to them. The staff here do an amazing job, an absolutely amazing job to help us and to put this on for us every week. If we can't speak to them, we'll speak to other members of the group because we're all like-minded. We're all from the same kind of background. Even if we're army, navy, RAF, it doesn't matter. "You've got Falklands veterans here. You've got Iraq veterans. Afghanistan veterans and there's all different backgrounds from all different regiments. You've got infantry regiments, non-infantry regiments. They're all veterans but we're all here as a family." Aaronson and Muharemović were greeted in the East Stand by the veterans and along with Foundation and club staff paid tribute with a short Remembrance ceremony. "Remembrance is a massive thing for everybody," said Derek. "You might not have served, but you might have had a family member that served that you're remembering. It's great to get players down. Obviously, they wear the shirts with poppies, and it gives them a perspective of what they're wearing that poppy for, in remembrance to our fallen comrades." The group then made its way to the Gary Speed Suite for a chat about how the veterans and the players could relate their respective experiences of representing their country, working in a team and bonding as tight-knit groups. A veteran spoke of being part of something bigger than himself and discovering a brotherhood, while Aaronson agreed that making everyone feel included in a team was an important step in building something special with a team. Veterans were then able to meet the players for photos as the visit came to a close. Aaronson said: "It was amazing to hear their stories and share our experiences too. They've made this country what it is today, I have a lot of respect for veterans and people who have sacrificed their lives for their country." The free weekly sessions run exclusively for veterans and include free breakfast sandwiches and hot drinks. There are also monthly trips and activities away from the stadium, as well as regular guest speakers. There is no need to book into the drop-in sessions but for more information email fitleeds@leedsunited.com or call 0113 367 6598.

item.title: Malik Willis going on IR can cost the Packers a round in the 2027 draft
item.description: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s compensatory pick formula is a little complicated, but to boil it down: Players are awarded points for their average salary over the life of the contract that they signed in free agency and receive playing-time bonuses based on the percentage of snaps they play during the regular season. If you lose players worth more points than the ones you sign, you get a draft pick from the NFL (which essentially mints an extra round of the draft, awarding 32 picks from the third to seventh rounds). That’s why the news of Malik Willis, a former Green Bay Packers quarterback, going on injured reserve impacts Green Bay in 2027. Already, Over The Cap has adjusted Willis’ compensatory draft pick projection to be a fourth-round pick, rather than the third-round pick he was initially expected to earn for the Packers. Willis was already a borderline third-round case (there are only two players currently set to earn third-round compensatory picks: edge defenders Jaelen Phillips and Trey Hendrickson), but losing at least four games of action is essentially a nail in the coffin for that selection. So instead of having what was projected to be the 98th pick in the draft for the loss of Willis, the Packers are now projected to receive the 133rd pick, according to Over The Cap. Former Packers leaving Green Bay haven’t had much luck this year. Offensive tackle Rasheed Walker, who was expected to net the Packers at least a fifth-round pick in free agency, overplayed his hand and signed late — leaving him with just a one-year deal. At the moment, the Packers are not expected to be awarded a pick for the loss of Walker. On top of that, receiver Romeo Doubs, who had a chance to earn Green Bay a fourth-round pick, is also on the injured reserve, which likely means that the Packers will only get a fifth-round pick for losing him. Overall, here’s the breakdown of the current outlook for the Packers’ compensatory picks in 2027: 4th round (Malik Willis) 5th round (Quay Walker) 5th round (Romeo Doubs) 6th round (Kingsley Enagbare) Teams are capped at four compensatory draft picks, or Walker (seventh round) would have been in play — had the team not canceled out that selection with the addition of cornerback Benjamin St-Juste in free agency. As a reminder, the Packers own their original draft picks outside of the first (Micah Parsons trade) and sixth (Darian Kinnard trade) rounds. They will also get the Cowboys’ fourth-round pick (Rashan Gary trade) and the Eagles’ sixth-round pick (Dontayvion Wicks trade) in 2027, bringing their overall total to 11 picks.

item.title: No Bull thoughts on the ILB room after the Daiyan Henley trade
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers walks onto the field before an NFL game against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve been hammering the Broncos on their reluctance to upgrade the inside linebacker position for years. No serious draft picks spent on it, no trades, and no serious free agent pursuit. One of the most overlooked reasons that our 2015 defense was so dominant was the quality of talent we had at ILB. We had Danny Trevathan and Brandon Marshall. Both of those guys could cover. Both defended the run. They were playmakers just like everyone else on that defense. The Broncos signing Daiyan Henley is an A+ move, and I darn near would give them the same grade if they had traded a 3rd-round pick for him. Henley is a player that has been loved and respected in the Chargers’ locker room. He’s a captain of the team. He’s also a guy who has worn the green dot for the defense (calling the plays for the defense). This is yet another high-character player added to a locker room built on high character and positive culture. Athletically, he’s the most talented linebacker on the inside we have seen in a very long time. His capability at coverage is excellent. He’s also a more sure tackler than either of our current starters. So the question for this team becomes: what happens with our defense? While I think he’s a real option for the future captain of our defense over Alex Singleton, that day will not be soon. He’s going to have to learn the defense and be in the system a while before the Broncos can even think of that. I expect him to be in the mix in nickel downs coming out of the bye. I think he’s likely going to take Justin Strnad’s spot as the starter before the season is over. No matter what happens with the snap count, having depth at inside linebacker is a big deal. Having a linebacker who can cover running backs in the flat and tight ends could very well be the missing piece for this defense to take a big step forward. I mean, to me that’s one of the important things in coaching, a mark of a great coach, is the ability to adapt to your personnel, your circumstances, the opponent, all those things, and have a system built that’s able to do that,” Harbaugh said. “And Dennard and the whole coaching staff have done a great job of that.” Six lessons learned from NFL Week 9: Arvell Reese a superstar in the making | CBSSports.com The biggest question surrounding Reese during the build-up to the NFL Draft was “Where do you play him?” The answer should have been another question: “Why does it matter?” And the Giants were exactly right to take that approach. Reese was an EDGE at Ohio State who moonlighted at off-ball linebacker. When the Giants initially drafted him, John Harbaugh basically said he’d play linebacker but also move around. Through eight games, Reese has now played at least 30 snaps at seven different spots: right inside linebacker, left inside linebacker, right linebacker, right EDGE, left linebacker, middle linebacker and left EDGE. Here’s where the self-awareness portion comes in. The Giants knew neither they nor Reese had to have it figured out on Day 1. The Giants are in Year 1 under John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Reese is 21 years old. The world was (and still is!) their oyster to experiment. Reese looks phenomenal. The Giants are 5-2-1 despite having started three different quarterbacks, and players such as Reese give them a bright future, too. item.title: Pirates Mitch Keller reportedly healthy and throwing
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 02: Mitch Keller #23 of the Pittsburgh Pirates pitches in the first inning against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park on August 02, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Pirates were supposed to have one of the top rotations in baseball last season. While they were good, they were far from the best. Paul Skenes coming back to earth was a big reason for that, but another of the Bucs’ reasons was the season that veteran Mitch Keller had. He finished the year 6-8 with a 5.29 ERA, 1.37 WHIP and just 87 strikeouts, and the 30-year-old righty then finished the year on the 60-day injured list with a grade 3 muscle strain. Well, according to Pirates GM Ben Cherington, Keller is now healthy and throwing. And the Bucs will be looking for a bounce back year from the veteran hurler. Cherington said : “Bottom line, we need more from Mitch in 2027 to accomplish our goals,” Cherington said. “He knows that. That’s not putting pressure on anything. That’s just a fact. “I’m saying that because I believe he can do that. We know the talent that’s there. We know the competitor that’s there. We have to do the work to help him. He has to do the work to put himself in that position to deliver more. … I’m excited about what Mitch will do for the Pirates in 2027.” Keller is signed through 2028 for the Bucs and is scheduled to make $18 million next season and $20 million the year after that. My guess is the Bucs are hoping Keller responds this year with a better performance, then might deal him if so. Either way, this is a pivotal upcoming season for Keller. It will likely have a huge role in whether or not he stays in Pittsburgh and whether or not the Pirates faith in him will be rewarded in any way. In addition, with Braxton Ashcraft coming into his own and the Seth Hernandez watch getting ready to begin proper, the sand is slowly slipping out of the hourglass for Keller. The upcoming season very well could tell the tale of the rest of his career. Either way, he is healthy, throwing, and reportedly ready for 2027.

item.title: Jobe Bellingham on his first England senior call up and the chance to play with brother Jude
item.description: Jobe Bellingham on his first England senior call up and the chance to play with brother Jude Jobe Bellingham has described earning his first senior England call-up alongside brother Jude as a “special” moment for his family. The Borussia Dortmund midfielder has been included in Thomas Tuchel’s latest squad after previously representing England at youth level. “I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” he said. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great. “To be called up for England is a dream itself and I’ve been so proud to have the opportunity to represent England at every age group. “I always enjoyed coming away with England, I love competing against top players at whichever age group. “But to have that chance of an opportunity to represent England with my brother, it’s really hard to put into words. “I don’t have the words, really. I think it’s only emotion that could describe it, and, hopefully, if that time does come, you’ll see a lot of emotion from people, and definitely from my family.” The 21-year-old revealed he learned of his selection after receiving a message from Tuchel while driving home from training. “Yeah, I’d been obviously hoping for it, as you would as a player,” he added. “It’s somewhere you aspire to be but I thought I’d probably be with the Under-21s, which I’m proud about in itself. “Then it was last Thursday when I was driving back from training, and I saw a message pop up in my car and it said, ‘Hi, Jobe, it’s Thomas Tuchel.’ “I was, as you can imagine, ecstatic and so excited and then when I took the call later on, it was just quite surreal. “You don’t really know what to do with yourself in that moment, but you’re just so pleased and I couldn’t stop smiling. “I feel really, really proud. It was something that I’d hoped for and I felt like I was making it a little bit more possible each week with each game, so yeah, I’m really pleased.”

item.description: BOWLING GREEN — Kent State 's postseason hopes vanished in the blink of an eye. Nakai Amachree's 48-yard touchdown run with 1:51 left lifted Bowling Green to a 33-28 win over the Golden Flashes on Nov. 10 at Doyt Perry Stadium. item.title: “Fell Flat On His Face” – Kevin O’Connor Slams Jaylen Brown’s Performance After “Manufacturing” Beef With Jayson Tatum and Getting Outplayed by Trade Partner Paul George
item.description: Jaylen Brown © X/ @Sixers Jaylen Brown and the Philadelphia 76ers found themselves on the wrong end of a blowout when they lost 123-101 to the Boston Celtics on Tuesday. In the case of Brown, he got outperformed in the stat sheets by his former running mate Jayson Tatum, with whom he’d verbally sparred in the weeks leading up to the Sixers-Celtics matchup. For analyst Kevin O’Connor, Tuesday night was a resounding loss for the former Finals MVP. “Downright terrible game by Jaylen Brown. His worst game of the year in the biggest moment with Philly. Tries to manufacture a rivalry with Jayson Tatum and he fell flat on his face. All while getting outplayed not only by Tatum but Paul George – the player the Celtics preferred,” O’Connor wrote on his X. In the Sixers’ first regular-season matchup against the Celtics this year, Brown was limited to 13 points on nine field goal attempts. He also had the most turnovers on his team (a total of four miscues). Meanwhile, Tatum put up 21 points on 8-for-17 FG shooting, along with six rebounds, four assists, and two blocks. He had plenty of help from 36-year-old Paul George, who went off for 36 points on a scintillating 63.6% shooting clip. It was George, of course, who was the centerpiece of the Sixers’ package to acquire Brown from Boston. While the consensus opinion at the time was that Philadelphia had won the trade, the Tatum-George tandem has now propelled the Celtics to the top spot in the Eastern Conference. Jaylen Brown Comments on Giving Jayson Tatum Cold Shoulder Prior to Tip-off Adding another layer of drama to the Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum beef was the cold-shoulder moment right before the game began. A viral clip shows Tatum attempting to embrace Brown, who barely acknowledged the gesture. After the game, Brown commented on this moment. (via Kris Rhim’s X) “I’m just focused on coming out and doing what’s best for my team…Credit to Jayson, he played well.” There’s no telling whether Brown and Tatum’s dynamic will drastically change by the time their teams lock horns again on Jan. 21. After that, there will be at least two more meetings between the Celtics and the Sixers before the regular season comes to an end.
